title: Acute food crises are concentrating where conflict, displacement, climate shocks, and response-financing gaps compound
source_unit: FAO, WFP, Global Network Against Food Crises, Global Report on Food Crises 2026
geography: 47 countries and territories analyzed for acute food insecurity in 2025, with global food-crisis, displacement, conflict, climate, and humanitarian-response comparisons

observations.period: 2025; Global Report on Food Crises 2026 assessment

denominator.unit: countries and territories analyzed for high levels of acute food insecurity

people_high_acute_food_insecurity.unit: people facing IPC/CH Phase 3 or above or equivalent in 2025

share_assessed_population.unit: percent of the analyzed population facing high acute food insecurity in 2025

people_facing_phase5.unit: people facing the most severe acute food-insecurity level in 2025

decade_pattern.value: acute hunger has approximately doubled over the past decade

observations.method: Joint FAO, WFP, and Global Network Against Food Crises synthesis using IPC/Cadre Harmonisé and equivalent acute food-insecurity classifications for crisis-affected countries and territories.
observations.uncertainty: The assessment covers countries with available crisis data rather than the entire world population; conflict access, funding cuts, and missing data limit comparability and timely measurement.
observations.subgroup: People in food-crisis countries, rural and urban households, children, displaced populations, conflict-affected communities, and populations classified across IPC/CH severity phases.
observations.counterinterpretation: The number and share can move with improved access, harvests, humanitarian delivery, or changing assessment coverage; aggregate crisis measures do not describe every household’s food access or coping strategy.

denominator.unit: people facing high acute food insecurity in the 2025 assessment

driver_set.value: conflict and insecurity, economic shocks, weather extremes, and forced displacement

largest_country_concentration.unit: countries accounting for approximately two-thirds of all people facing high acute hunger

protracted_crisis_pattern.value: 35 countries and territories have appeared in every Global Report on Food Crises for nine years

persistent_crisis_share.unit: percent or more of people in IPC/CH Phase 3 or above living in the protracted-crisis contexts identified by FAO

observations.method: GRFC 2026 synthesis of acute food-insecurity drivers, country concentration, and repeated crisis presence across the report series.
observations.uncertainty: Driver categories overlap and are not additive causal estimates; country concentration reflects assessed populations and does not imply that other countries are free of risk.
observations.subgroup: Conflict-affected populations, displaced people, climate-exposed communities, food producers, local markets, humanitarian actors, and governments in protracted crises.
observations.counterinterpretation: Protracted presence can reflect better monitoring as well as persistent need; prevention, livelihoods investment, peacebuilding, and local food production may alter crisis trajectories.

simultaneous_famines.unit: famine conditions confirmed in parts of the Gaza Strip and Sudan during 2025

famine_risk_2026.value: risk persists for the Gaza Strip, Sudan, and South Sudan in 2026

hotspot_mechanism.value: conflict, displacement, market disruption, climate shocks, and constrained humanitarian access can move populations from chronic vulnerability into acute crisis

observations.method: GRFC 2026 global assessment and outlook using acute food-insecurity and famine classifications plus partner analysis of crisis drivers and access.
observations.uncertainty: Famine confirmation and outlooks depend on rapidly changing access, mortality, food-consumption, and livelihood evidence; risk is not the same as occurrence.
observations.subgroup: Populations in Gaza, Sudan, South Sudan, and other hunger hotspots; displaced households; children; health and nutrition systems; and humanitarian responders.
observations.counterinterpretation: Early warning, negotiated access, food assistance, agricultural support, and conflict de-escalation can prevent forecast deterioration; famine risk does not establish an inevitable endpoint.

denominator.unit: global humanitarian and food-crisis response system described by FAO, WFP, and partners

funding_pattern.value: humanitarian and food-security response funding has retreated toward levels last seen nearly a decade ago

response_constraint.value: funding cuts and limited access to conflict areas have contributed to the lowest availability of food-crisis data in a decade

response_shift.value: prevention, resilience, and agricultural solutions must be sequenced alongside food and nutrition assistance

observations.method: GRFC 2026 and partner response analysis linking humanitarian financing, access, data availability, prevention, resilience, and agricultural livelihoods.
observations.uncertainty: Funding comparisons depend on definitions, inflation, appeal coverage, and reporting periods; a financing decline does not measure the effectiveness of every response or local adaptation.
observations.subgroup: Humanitarian agencies, donors, national authorities, farmers, local organizations, displaced populations, and communities in recurrent crisis.
observations.counterinterpretation: Better targeting, local leadership, early action, and agricultural investments may improve outcomes even when aggregate funding is constrained; short-term aid and resilience programs are complements, not substitutes in every setting.

related_sources.claim: FAO publication page and report framing for the 2026 Global Report on Food Crises.
WFP global hunger-crisis page provides complementary conflict, displacement, and acute-hunger context.
FAO 2026 emergency and resilience appeal adds prevention, resilience, agriculture, and financing context.

boundary: This record adds acute food-crisis, conflict, displacement, climate-shock, famine-risk, data-access, and response-financing evidence. It is not the same indicator as SOFI chronic hunger or healthy-diet affordability, does not estimate individual consumption, and does not use respondent-level microdata.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official WFP, FAO, and partner pages for the Global Report on Food Crises 2026 and the FAO emergency appeal were reviewed; acute-hunger scale, drivers, country concentration, famine risk, funding, access, and prevention claims were cross-checked.
